tools.name: progress
tools.description: Reports the work left in this turn, for the progress display only. Use it during work that will take more than a few steps when you keep no task list: start in your first response that calls tools, with a rough guess if that is all you have, and send it in the same response as your other tool calls, never on its own. List the items in order, the one you are on first, each in a few words (5 at most). Give each a size: s — a quick change or lookup, about 1–2 tool calls; m — a few files or a few rounds, 3–8; l — a broad change or a debugging loop, 9 or more. When running a command is the item (a test suite, a build), give `run` with the exact command instead of a size. Send `{done: 1}` with the first tool calls of the next item, one item at a time and not the list again: a late `done`, or one for several items, loses their times. Send `left` only when items are added, dropped or changed. Once the last item is done, just answer: the turn ending closes it. Returns `ok`.

script: tool.call Bash rm -rf build && git push --force origin main
